title: Power-up time capsules: top-right gauges showing time left on active timed power-ups
description:
## Problem / goal
Timed power-ups (today: Super-Sizer, which widens the paddle for a while) give no feedback about how long they have left. Show each active timed power-up as a "time capsule" in the top-right corner that drains as its time runs out.

## Behaviour
- Each active timed effect gets one capsule, stacked vertically in the top-right corner, below the HUD's sector label (sim-a7k.2) if present. Space for up to 3 at once, newest at the bottom.
- A capsule shows:
  - the power-up's icon (today the shared `powerup.png`)
  - a pill-shaped gauge whose fill drains left-to-right, in proportion to the remaining time
  - the seconds left, e.g. `6.2s`
- Steelbreak HUD style: cyan `#4fd8ff` fill on a dark `#16202c` pill, thin light outline. The fill turns amber `#ffab4d` and blinks in the last 2 s.
- Picking up the same power-up again refreshes its timer: the capsule refills in place and no duplicate appears.
- When an effect expires, its capsule disappears and the others close the gap.
- **Pause:** capsules freeze while paused (the effect timers already do).
- **New run / level:** capsules clear on a new run and on a level change (they follow `ActiveEffects`).
- Non-timed power-ups (none exist yet) get no capsule.

## Out of scope
New power-ups, per-kind icons (follow-up art), capsule art from the art pipeline (shapes/UI nodes first), sounds.

## Notes for the coder
- Drive everything from `ActiveEffects` (`src/powerups/mod.rs`), which already holds each effect's `kind` and `Timer`. The capsule system reads it every frame, so no extra bookkeeping is needed and expiry is automatic, matching the "recompute from ActiveEffects" pattern in CLAUDE.md.
- Bevy UI (`Node`) anchored top-right, run-scoped (`DespawnOnExit(AppState::InGame)`).
- Headless test: insert effects into `ActiveEffects` and assert the capsule count, order and fill fraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Catching Super-Sizer shows a capsule in the top-right with the power-up icon, a full cyan gauge and the seconds remaining; the gauge drains as time passes.
- [ ] In the last 2 s the gauge turns amber and blinks; when the effect ends the capsule disappears.
- [ ] Catching Super-Sizer again while active refills the same capsule (no second capsule).
- [ ] With 2–3 timed effects active (test-injected), the capsules stack top-right in pickup order, and closing a gap works when a middle one expires.
- [ ] Pausing freezes the capsules; a new run starts with none.
- [ ] `cargo test` covers count/order/fill from `ActiveEffects`; clippy and `trunk build` pass.

title: Parallax background: in-house slow-drifting layers behind the playfield
description:
## Problem / goal
The background is one flat image. Add depth with a parallax background: several layers drifting slowly at different speeds behind the playfield.

## Decisions (user, 2026-09-28)
- **In-house:** `bevy-parallax` was evaluated and rejected. Its latest release targets Bevy 0.14 (GitHub master reaches 0.15; we're on 0.19), and it's driven by camera movement, while our camera is fixed.
- **Motion:** slow ambient drift only. Each layer drifts continuously at its own speed/direction; deeper layers move slower.
- **Art:** a new layered art brief (sim-73n-dependent, filed alongside). The code ships with placeholder layers first.
- **Backlog:** parked until the playfield-frame interview (sim-73n) settles resolution and the visible area.

## Behaviour (draft)
- 3–4 layers behind everything (e.g. deep space/stars, far trusses, near girders/lamps, dust/haze), each an image that tiles seamlessly in its drift direction.
- Each layer drifts at a configured speed (px/s) and direction, wrapping forever with no visible seam or jump.
- Visible on the main menu, settings and in game. Keeps drifting while paused (ambient; not gameplay).
- Layer list defined in one place (config struct or a small `assets/parallax/*.ron`): image, z-order, speed, direction, opacity. A future per-level skin (sim-a7k roadmap) can swap it.
- Replaces the single hangar background sprite (sim-rdl.6 placeholder / sim-aww).
- Works on web.

## Out of scope
Paddle-follow shift, event-reactive speed-ups (later explorations), a camera-driven parallax, the art itself.

## Notes for the coder
- `src/parallax/` with its own `Plugin`, registered from `main()` (renderer-dependent; the headless tests use `MinimalPlugins`).
- Use `Sprite` with `image_mode: SpriteImageMode::Tiled { .. }` sized to the visible area, and scroll by offsetting within a one-tile period (translate and wrap), or by an equivalent UV offset. Keep the wrap maths a pure fn and unit-test it.
- Sizes come from the playfield-frame outcome (sim-73n).

## Open until the frame interview
Exact visible area, layer count, speeds.

A power-up that **rearranges the bricks** in the level, with a visible animation (the bricks visibly move or shuffle rather than teleporting).

- Particles (bevy_enoki, sim-pdp) are available for the visual trail.

## Open questions for the interview
- Shuffle how: a random permutation of the remaining bricks, a mirror or rotation, gravity (bricks fall to fill gaps), or a slide toward the paddle?
- Good for the player (clears paths, groups weak bricks) or chaos/neutral?
- Animation length, and does the game pause or slow during it? What happens to the ball meanwhile?
- Does it interact with the neighbour-combo epic (filed alongside), e.g. rearranging to create combos?

## Problem / goal

- Losing the last life or clearing all bricks goes to `GameOver`, with a won/lost outcome kept in a resource; the existing text is shown; R starts a new run.
- A new run always resets score to 0 and lives to 3 (one constant); the lives label is driven by that constant. `RestartGame` is still broadcast so power-ups reset themselves.

Any new menu UI (next tasks), settings, audio.

title: Serialize native GUI runs on the shared X display (lock script, unique window titles, clean teardown)
description:
## Problem / goal
All agent roles share one X display (WSLg `DISPLAY=:0`), and every native window is titled "Breakout". Concurrent native runs from different roles (the coder's `timeout cargo run` smoke checks, and a duplicate tester session) sent input to and killed each other's windows, and left an orphaned `target/debug/sim` with PPID=1. Testers lost time retrying, and some criteria were only partly verified live. Make native runs exclusive, identifiable and cleanly torn down, and give the tester standard tooling.

## Behaviour
- New `scripts/native-run.sh [--label <text>] [--wait <secs>] [-- <extra cargo args>]`: the only sanctioned way for any agent to launch the native game.
  - Takes an exclusive `flock` on a shared lock file (e.g. `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/breakout-display-0.lock`, keyed by `$DISPLAY`) for the whole run. It writes a holder record next to it: role (`$AGENT_ACTOR`), label/issue, pid, start time.
  - If the lock is held, it waits up to `--wait` seconds (default 0 = fail fast). Otherwise it exits non-zero with a message naming the current holder, e.g. `display :0 busy: tester@tester (sim-rdl.2) pid 1234 since 23:10:05`. A duplicate role instance therefore gets a clear, logged refusal instead of silently cross-talking.
  - The game runs with a unique window title: `Breakout [<actor> <label>]`.
  - It runs the game in its own process group. On script exit, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or `timeout`, it kills the whole group (cargo plus the `sim` child) and releases the lock, so no process is left reparented to init.
  - Prints the window title, and the X window id once mapped (via `xdotool search --sync --name`), so drivers target that exact window.
- The game reads an optional `BREAKOUT_WINDOW_TITLE` env var for the window title, native only. The default stays "Breakout". Wasm is unaffected.
- `.claude/workflow.yaml`, `functional.run`: replace the bare `cargo run` with `scripts/native-run.sh --label <issue-id>`. Add a note that drivers must use xdotool/wmctrl against the printed window id, never a name search for plain "Breakout".
- `docs/agent-workflow.md` (or a short `scripts/README.md`): how to run, drive (`xdotool key --window <id>`, `xdotool mousemove --window`), screenshot (`import -window <id>` / `xwd`) and why. Also note that the coder never launches the native game.

## Duplicate role instances
The `agent-team` launcher already refuses to start a role whose tmux window exists. The duplicate tester that caused the sim-v0i.2/.3 incidents was a session started outside the launcher. In this repo, the display lock above is the guard: a second instance can't drive `:0` and is told who holds it. Changes to the launcher (`~/.local/bin/agent-team`) and to the agent definitions live outside this repo and are out of scope for the coder; the pm tracks them with the user.

## Out of scope
Xvfb / per-worktree X servers, CI GUI runs, changes to `~/.local/bin/agent-team` or `~/.claude/agents/*`.

## Notes for the coder
- Pure tooling plus one tiny code change (`main()` window title from env inside the existing `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` area). No gameplay change.
- Process-group kill: `setsid` the child (or `set -m`), `trap 'kill -- -$pgid' EXIT INT TERM`; `flock -n` / `flock -w` on fd 9.
- `xdotool`, `wmctrl`, `xwd` and `import` are installed on this machine (user, 2026-09-27); the script should still fail with a clear message if xdotool is missing.
- shellcheck-clean if shellcheck is available.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `scripts/native-run.sh --label demo` opens the game with window title `Breakout [<actor> demo]` and prints its X window id.
- [x] While one run is live, a second `scripts/native-run.sh --label other` (from another worktree/shell) exits non-zero immediately with a message naming the holder (actor, label, pid); with `--wait 30` it starts once the first run ends.
- [x] Ending a run by closing the window, Ctrl-C, or `timeout 10 scripts/native-run.sh` leaves no `sim` or `cargo` process behind (`pgrep -f target/debug/sim` is empty) and releases the lock (a new run starts at once).
- [x] `xdotool key --window <printed id> p` pauses that game window, confirmed by `import -window <id>` screenshots before and after.
- [x] Plain `cargo run` still shows the title "Breakout"; `trunk build` succeeds (the env-var title is native-only).
- [x] `.claude/workflow.yaml` `functional.run` uses the script, and the driving/screenshot how-to is documented in the repo.
- [x] `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass.
